**Finding: deviation (critical) — Article XIII, ¶p0130**

The limitation of liability runs entirely one way:

- **Exclusion of damages (a)** protects only Licensor ("IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE TO LICENSEE OR TO ANY THIRD PARTY...").
- **Cap (b)** caps only Licensor, at "ONE HALF OF THE AMOUNT PAID BY THE LICENSEE" — below even the walk-away floor of six months' fees, and measured on amounts *paid* only.
- **Our client is uncapped**, with a broad one-way indemnity in Article XII (¶p0128–p0129) sitting outside any limitation.
- **No carve-outs** for confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement; ¶p0131 reinforces the section as a Licensor-only inducement.

Redline validated (ok:true) with minimal edits to the two existing sentences: exclusion and cap made mutual, cap reset to the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, an "Excluded Claims" super-cap sentence added, and confirmation that Licensee's fee obligations are not damages for cap purposes. Fallback offered in the comment is a mutual 12-month fee cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

One residual item worth raising in negotiation (outside this rule's minimal edit): the tail of (a) also purports to disclaim all Licensor liability for IP infringement claims, which cuts against the IP carve-out we have added.
